subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
subtype: Approach: weekly schedule with time blocks [Action]
passage: My name is Salma, and every Sunday evening I do the same thing with a calendar and a cup of tea. Classes go in first, in blue. Then two study blocks a day, meals at fixed times, the gym three days, and seven hours for sleep. What I learned the hard way is to leave gaps. Every day has a forty-minute empty block after lunch, and there is one free evening each week. Last month a project meeting ran over, and the empty block took the hit, so nothing else moved. My roommate Hansa saw the calendar and copied the layout. By Friday we both agreed the week felt calmer than it looked on paper.

qa.q: How many hours of sleep did Salma block each day?
qa.a: Salma blocked seven hours for sleep.

qa.q: How did Salma feel about the week by Friday?
qa.a: Salma felt calmer, and Hansa felt the same. The gaps in the schedule kept the week from feeling crowded. 😊

qa.q: What could Salma add if the empty blocks keep getting used up, and why?
qa.a: Salma could move one study block to the free evening and make a quick note of why it slipped, since a repeating problem shows the plan needs a change.

qa.q: How might Hansa see the calendar when copying it?
qa.a: Hansa probably sees a clear plan that leaves space for surprises, so it looks easier to follow than a packed timetable.

grounding: A student blocks classes, study, meals, gym and sleep in a weekly calendar and keeps gaps for surprises.
